title: Split net/buffers into one file per class

pr.title: net: one file per class, namespace net::detail becomes net
pr.description:
`include/net/buffers.h` and `src/net/buffers.cpp` grew to five classes. This moves each one into its own header and source file: `buffer`, `buffer_pool`, `send_ring`, `frames`, and `debug`. The namespace `net::detail` becomes `net`, because these types are the public API of the library now. The tests move the same way, with the shared helpers in `tests/test_util.h`.

No behavior change: the code moves as is. The server files change only their includes and the namespace.

bugs.note: One-token change inside a moved block: Buffer::view() now checks len against capacity_ - offset instead of size_ - offset, so it returns bytes past the written part. BufferPool reuses buffers across clients and reset() keeps the old bytes, so a client that sends a ping header with a long length and no payload gets a frame of stale bytes from other clients echoed back. The test helper sizes each buffer exactly, so the tests cannot see it.

traps.why: The index mask is wrong for a capacity that is not a power of two, but the only caller, the unchanged Connection, passes config.sendRing, and the unchanged loadConfig() refuses a send_ring that is not a power of two from 2 to 1024.

commit() adds n to size_ without a check against the capacity, but the only caller, the unchanged Connection::onReadable(), passes the result of recv() into writable(), which is at most writable().size().

The frame span points into the buffer, and consume() moves those bytes, which looks like a dangling span, but the unchanged Connection::onReadable() hands each frame to the handler before it calls consume().
